extracted.intended_audience: general readers, artists, critics, and students of aesthetics seeking criteria for evaluating or producing art
extracted.subtask_description: Provide criteria for understanding, evaluating, and producing art in the Tolstoyan sense — focusing on transmission of feeling, sincerity, moral worth of subject-matter, accessibility, and clarity of expression. Useful for writers, artists, critics, and readers who want a practical standard for what counts as 'art'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as transmission of feeling (the test of infection)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The object of this activity is to transmit to others feeling the artist has experienced... The test of art is infection. If an author has moved you so that you feel as he felt... the work that has so infected you is a work of art."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a work by whether it intentionally and successfully causes other people to experience the feeling the artist had; a work that does not re-evoke the author's feeling in others is not art. Scoring note: focus on internal response (shared feeling) rather than external features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intention to communicate (art begins with purpose to infect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art begins when someone, with the object of making others share his feeling, expresses his feeling by certain external indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between spontaneous contagious behaviour (e.g., yawning) and deliberate artistic expression intended to produce shared feeling. A creator must intend to transmit feeling, not merely display emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate expression / clarity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Without adequate expression there is no art, for there is no infection, no transference to others of the author's feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the form (movements, lines, colours, sounds, words) used by the artist is clear and effective enough to 'infect' the audience. Anti-patterns: obscure, muddled, or overly abstruse expression that prevents shared feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity (authenticity of feeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: The one great quality which makes a work of art truly contagious is its sincerity. If an artist is really actuated by a feeling... and is strongly impelled to communicate that feeling... then he will not be satisfied till he has found a clear way of expressing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the feeling expressed appears genuine and originates in the artist (not borrowed or calculated). Scoring guidance: insincere or simulated feeling produces a resistance and fails to infect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (not borrowing feelings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The man who is not borrowing his feelings, but has drawn what he expresses from the depths of his nature, is sure to be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence that the feelings expressed arise from the creator's own depths rather than imitation of fashionable sentiments or market trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter must be spreadable feelings (what art transmits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject-matter of art consists of feelings which can be spread from man to man, feelings which are 'contagious' or 'infectious.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the content centers on feelings that can be shared across people, rather than abstract doctrinal assertions or purely technical displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral/ethical quality of subject-matter (religious perception / promotion of brotherhood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is valuable or objectionable in proportion as it is serviceable or harmful to mankind... The religious perception of our time... is the consciousness that our well-being... lies in the growth of brotherhood among men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the feelings transmitted tend to promote human well‑being, brotherhood, compassion, or at least do not hinder progress toward well‑being. Tolstoy divides acceptable subject-matter into (1) feelings from the highest perception of our relation to others and the Source, and (2) simple harmless feelings of common life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality / accessibility (art should reach the many, not a narrow elite)
rubrics_metrics.description: A work of art that united every one with the author, and with one another, would be perfect art... the more nearly a work of art approaches such expression of feeling that everyone may be infected by it—the nearer it approaches perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work can move people of different social classes and levels of development (Tolstoy emphasizes 'unperverted country peasants' as a test). Anti-patterns: art that only delights a narrow 'cultured' crowd or requires specialized training to be moved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of mere physiological effects or intellectual puzzles
rubrics_metrics.description: They will mistake for art something that produces a merely physiological effect—lulling or exciting them; or some intellectual puzzle that gives them something to think about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate works that merely arouse sensation or intellectual amusement from those that genuinely transmit a human feeling. Sensationalism, shock for its own sake, or clever puzzles are not, by themselves, art in this view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art is not identical with science but can transmit truths as feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Science investigates... Art transmits these truths from the region of perception to the region of emotion... The business of art lies to make that understood and felt which, in the form of an argument, might be incomprehensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that works may combine scientific/ideological content and art, but judge the artistic element by its success in turning knowledge or argument into felt experience. Do not conflate technical correctness with artistic success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal test over external authorities or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The test of art is internal... Very many people of our circle... have lost that simple feeling... and will always be mistaking other things for art, and seeking for external guides, such as the opinions of 'recognised authorities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the inward response of shared feeling as the criterion rather than critics' consensus, fashion, or temporary popularity. Beware of relying solely on institutional validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should not be produced primarily for money, fame, or private satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the artist produces art for money or fame—or the cultured only—this tends to corrupt the sincerity and universality of art... 'As soon as the author is not producing art for his own satisfaction—does not himself feel what he wishes to express—a resistance immediately springs up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creators' motives when possible; commercial or status-driven production risks producing inauthentic, non-contagious art. Note nuance: Tolstoy values an artist's own feeling, but condemns production aimed only at external rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works of art should not propagate harmful beliefs or reinforce false divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A false and antiquated view of life is supported by means of art... If the false view of life be destroyed this art will cease to appear valuable... A dominant church has utilised art to maintain its sway over men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether a work's transmitted feelings uphold harmful superstitions, sectarianism, hatred, patriotism that leads to war, or other divisive impulses. Anti-pattern: art that serves to sustain oppressive institutions or immoral ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value measured by serviceability or harm to mankind
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is a human activity, and consequently does not exist for its own sake, but is valuable or objectionable in proportion as it is serviceable or harmful to mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating art, consider practical social consequences of the feelings it spreads; high artistic merit includes contributing to human flourishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple, everyday feelings can be true art when harmless and widely shareable
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple feelings of common life, accessible to every one—provided that they are such as do not hinder progress towards well-being... This branch includes all harmless jokes, folk-stories, nursery rhymes...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discount 'primitive' or popular forms; evaluate whether their feelings are genuine, harmless, and transmissible across people.
